scoring_note: Editorial musical hypotheses, not calibrated listeners. Specialist lane is proposed/inactive until routing and catalog activation are separately approved.

songs.title: Blitzkrieg Bop
songs.rationale: The chant and the rush are the point: an instantaneous communal jolt with no narrative detour.

songs.title: London Calling
songs.rationale: An outward-looking warning on a grander arrangement, asking for critical attention as well as motion.

songs.title: Anarchy in the U.K.
songs.rationale: An openly confrontational proclamation that measures appetite for threat and public provocation.

songs.title: Holiday in Cambodia
songs.rationale: Fierce satire places an abrasive political viewpoint above uncomplicated group release.

songs.title: Ever Fallen in Love (With Someone You Shouldn't've)
songs.rationale: A brisk melodic heartbreak song where raw speed conceals emotional doubt.

songs.title: New Rose
songs.rationale: An unpolished first-wave adrenaline surge with little interest in extended argument.

songs.title: Teenage Kicks
songs.rationale: Young romance wins over menace; a direct, buoyant melodic foil for ideological punk.

songs.title: Los Angeles
songs.rationale: An ugly, unsparing portrait of a place, driven by roots-inflected speed and observational friction.

songs.title: Rise Above
songs.rationale: A clenched communal refusal, engineered for collective resistance more than private doubt.

songs.title: Straight Edge
songs.rationale: A tiny manifesto of self-discipline delivered with radical speed and personal command.

songs.title: Banned in D.C.
songs.rationale: Virtuosic hardcore volatility tests the attraction of dramatic pivots inside extreme speed.

songs.title: Oh Bondage Up Yours!
songs.rationale: A confrontational, sax-laced blast of feminism that wants to change the argument, not just the tempo.

songs.title: Basket Case
songs.rationale: Radio-bright velocity carries anxious self-doubt, upending the expectation that speed means certainty.

songs.title: Typical Girls
songs.rationale: Elastic rhythms and social critique make a long, exploratory argument rather than a straight-line attack.

songs.title: 12 X U
songs.rationale: Bare rhythmic abrasion and formal economy privilege cut-to-the-bone energy over complexity.

songs.title: Alternative Ulster
songs.rationale: An urgent, place-specific call for change turns guitar attack into collective political expression.

songs.title: Ruby Soho
songs.rationale: Ska-inflected camaraderie makes streetwise punk singable and emotionally inviting.

songs.title: Self Esteem
songs.rationale: Blunt guitars frame a confession of romantic capitulation, separating loudness from emotional control.

pairings.phrase: Three chords and a grin, or the end of the world on the radio?
pairings.why: The Ramones invite an instant shout; The Clash put a larger, more observant warning inside the charge.

pairings.phrase: Start a chant, or start an argument nobody can stop?
pairings.why: Ramones favor uncomplicated shared ignition; Sex Pistols make provocation itself the central statement.

pairings.phrase: Riot outside the door, or heartbreak behind the grin?
pairings.why: The Pistols bark a public challenge; Buzzcocks keep the pace but expose personal doubt.

pairings.phrase: A poisoned postcard, or a crush that moves faster than thinking?
pairings.why: Dead Kennedys make satire dangerous; The Undertones turn speed into emotionally direct, lower-pressure pleasure.

pairings.phrase: Hit the first chord and run, or pull the whole song apart?
pairings.why: The Damned sprint on impact; The Slits dismantle the assumptions and structure along the way.

pairings.phrase: A messy city after midnight, or a life drawn in permanent marker?
pairings.why: X paint a tangled scene; Minor Threat reduce the question to disciplined immediate refusal.

pairings.phrase: Stand your ground, or admit the ground is moving?
pairings.why: Black Flag weaponize public certainty; Green Day make anxious vulnerability catchy and smoother.

pairings.phrase: A band that changes gears mid-flight, or a blade that never bends?
pairings.why: Bad Brains' dynamics keep mutating; Wire compress intensity into a briefer, harsher form.

pairings.phrase: Fight the script, or confess you're trapped inside it?
pairings.why: X-Ray Spex challenge the culture outward; Offspring direct their energy into private romantic self-criticism.

pairings.phrase: The siren outside, or friends singing all the way home?
pairings.why: The Clash expand political stakes; Rancid make the street-level story more communal and warm.

pairings.phrase: Unpick the machine slowly, or rip the warning label off?
pairings.why: The Slits make critique playful and exploratory; Dead Kennedys bring sharper, more immediate danger.

pairings.phrase: Demand a different future, or wonder why love keeps failing?
pairings.why: Stiff Little Fingers turn anger outward; Buzzcocks make the same speed carry vulnerable confusion.
